cases.setup: Provide a public Python checkout whose signature collector omits positional-only annotations, a positional-only-capable runtime, and the mixed-parameter reproduction.
checks: The assessment identifies concrete collector, runtime-gate, test-owner and analyzer-entry-point bindings with code-anchor hashes.
The public reproduction result records the unused-import diagnostic for the positional-only annotation import.
The assessment records the omitted AST category and differentiates it from ordinary and keyword-only collection.
Inspection does not alter tracked source files.

cases.setup: Provide a confirmed omission assessment and established runtime support policy with current collector and annotation-test bindings.
checks: The diff collects positional-only parameter names and annotations through the existing signature-analysis accumulators.
The diff retains existing ordinary and keyword-only collection and defaults processing.
AST field access is guarded where older supported runtimes require it.
A regression uses an imported name only in a positional-only parameter annotation and asserts no diagnostics.
Syntax-specific test handling prevents unsupported runtimes from executing the positional-only snippet.
Prior diagnostic and annotation-test observations are marked stale pending validation.

cases.setup: Provide the edited checkout and explicitly bound public reproduction and test commands. Include relevant adjacent annotation tests and the current runtime support policy.
checks: Rendered current argv commands correspond to public current checkout checks, not hidden or historical-only bindings.
The focused regression passes on a positional-only-capable runtime without an unused-import diagnostic.
The mixed positional-only and keyword-only reproduction produces no unused-import diagnostic for either annotation name.
The validation report records adjacent annotation test results and review of defaults, binding and runtime compatibility.
Unavailable compatibility or broader regression checks are recorded as UNKNOWN or unexecuted rather than PASS.
The report identifies tested scope and does not claim whole-project or cross-project acceptance from focused results.
